name: Yulong Audio
_the_lot_first_cited_a_brand_id_that_DOE: The records under this brand were first written citing a short brand id - « aune » and « yulong » - while this file's id is the long form. The helper ecrire_lot.fiche_marque() REFUSED to create a second brand file and named this one instead, which is exactly what it was written for: three times on 2026-11-25 a script that could not find a brand file at the name it guessed went on to CREATE one, producing the Cambridge Audio, Cyrus and MUSICIAN duplicates. Here the refusal came before any file was written, the device identities were corrected to this id, and no duplicate exists. The verifier's own « brand is not in database/brands » error caught the device side a moment later - two independent guards, one on the write and one on the read.
_terms_not_concluded: No terms page found on yulongaudio.com, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding none. Measured 2026-11-25: the site has exactly five sections - About Us, Products, News, Support, Contact Us - identical on both language trees, and none is legal. robots.txt returns 404 with the body « File not found », so no Content-Signal and no Claude group exist because the file does not. Footer: « Copyright (c) 2003-2017 All Rights Reserved Shenzhen Yu Long Yun Electronics Co., Ltd. » - the end date is nine years stale, which is itself a fact about how closely this site is maintained.
_HTTPS_is_unusable_on_this_host: yulongaudio.com, www.yulongaudio.com and daartaudio.com all fail TLS with « no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name », so the site is reachable only over plain HTTP and every URL under this brand is http://. yulong-audio.com, en.yulongaudio.com, daart.audio, yulongaudio.cn and da-art.com do not resolve. Second maker today invisible to any tool that upgrades to HTTPS, after MUSICIAN Audio Technology.
_the_catalogue_splits_in_two_and_there_a: The older models carry real specification TEXT in the page body; every newer model's product detail is nothing but JPEGs, with 42 characters of whitespace as the only text. And the Support page offers DRIVERS ONLY - eight files, every one a Windows USB driver - so for the image-only models there is no text fallback anywhere. The Chinese tree was checked and is the same images. Unlike Shanling, xDuoo, Sabaj and Aune, THIS image wall has no door.
_nine_models_absent_for_want_of_text: Aquila III, Aurora, DA1, DA11, D39, DA2, ASURA, A39 and DP1. The only maker-written text for them is the product TITLE, and one is tempting: « Aquila III PCM1536KHz DSD1024 DAC, Preamplifier and Headphone amplifier ». A device-level claim in a page title, no socket named, no surrounding sentence anywhere - it settles nothing about what an input accepts and no record was written from it. DP1 is in any case a digital interface, not a converter.
_models_that_exist_only_as_DRIVER_FILENA: No product page exists for the D200, the original DA8, the ADA1 or the U200. They survive only inside the Support page's filenames - « Canary+DA9+Aquila+D200+XMOS+Driver-v4.13.0.rar », « DA8 DA8II winX- win10 Driver 1062.exe », « ADA1 U200 Drive.rar ». Those filenames are the only maker-side confirmation that those four products ever existed, and they carry no specification.
_no_NOS_and_the_bypasses_are_something_e: The word NOS appears on no Yulong page in either language, and no model claims an oversampling-bypass or filter-OFF position. Two things ARE called bypasses and neither is one: the Aquila II's synchronous mode « bypassed the ASRC circuit within the ES9038Pro DAC », which is the resampler and not the interpolation filter, and the DA8 II's jitter-eliminator and volume-circuit bypasses. `correctable` is written on no Yulong record, and no Yulong model with text specs lists an I2S input.
